abstract: In this paper main information about fractal labyrinths is presented with fractional calculus mathematical apparatus inclusion. Also fractal labyrinths are explained as mathematical physics object. Methods of automatic fractal labyrinth synthesis with specified parameters are analyzed. Software is created for automate some laborious aspects in branching (labyrinth-like) fractals designing for different physical processes simulation. Comparative analysis is given for branching ultra wideband antennas versus some examples of classical "fractal antennas". Some conclusions are made about this approach compatibility for antennas geometry synthesis and the next steps are proposed to it further improvement.

articleTitle: Radar high resolution range profile recognition via Dual-SVDD classifier
abstract: To identify the out-of-database targets in the process of radar ground target recognition with high resolution range profile, this paper proposes an improved radar ground target classifier based on the covariance distribution of the space of training features, namely Dual-SVDD classifier. In the training phase, a double correlate SVDD structure is constructed in feature space and a multi-region data description is obtained based on the covariance of target training database. The new classifier separates the training sets into several regions, which are independent identically uniform distributed. Then, the category determination of testing target data is based on the support vectors and the region radial of the SVDD method with the multi-region data description. This method can work without the template of out-of-database samples, which improves the effectiveness of target identification. Finally, the experiment based on the measured data verifies its excellent performance of identification.

articleTitle: Metrics for quantifying cognitive radar performance
abstract: This work develops two metrics to help quantify the performance of a cognitive radar system; they are the combined cumulative squared deviation (CCSD) and the cumulative coherent processing interval (CCPI). The cognitive system is based on the fully adaptive radar (FAR) framework for cognition. Simulated and experimental results are provided for a single target tracking case where the pulse repetition frequency and number of pulses are adjusted to maintain tracker performance. The CCSD and CCPI are used to compare the simulated and experimental results for three different parameter selection methods as well as static parameter cases.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of airborne LFMCW-MIMO vitual array radar
abstract: In this paper, a new radar scheme is proposed that applies linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) signal to airborne multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) virtual array radar. The combined system, on one hand, facilitates transmission of LFMCW signal by using MIMO virtual array radar with separated transmit and receive arrays, on the other hand, compensate the power loss due to wide-beam illumination for the MIMO radar by transmitting LFMCW signal. We compare non-adaptive processing performance of the proposed system with that of another system, given the same array geometry, which transmits linear frequency modulated pulse(LFMP) signal. It is demonstrated that the proposed system has higher output signal to clutter plus noise ratio (SCNR) than the LFMP radar system, especially for targets with high velocity and small RCS.

articleTitle: An improved IMM algorithm based on maneuvering-adaptive model set
abstract: Interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm is one of the effective methods for maneuvering target tracking. The conventional IMM algorithm based on a fixed model set may lead to filter mismatch for a high maneuvering target. In this paper, an improved IMM algorithm is proposed by using maneuver-adaptive model set. Based on the maneuver detection and adaptively adjusting the process noise levels, it can effectively make a quick response when the maneuver occurs while it has a low root-mean-square error when the motion is relatively stable. Finally, some numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Passive ground camouflage target recognition based on gray feature and texture feature in SAR images
abstract: Recently, Synthetic Aperture Radar plays a significant role in military reconnaissance and battle damage assessment. However, comparing with optic image, SAR image interpretation is complex because of their imaging characteristics. Furthermore, it is more difficult to distinguish camouflage targets in SAR image. In this paper, we proposed a new method to recognize real targets and camouflage targets. On the basis of SAR images, we studied the difference between real targets and passive camouflage targets at first. Then, we extract gray feature and texture feature of all the targets in an image. Finally, targets were divided into two clusters by using K-means algorithm. The simulation result demonstrates feasibility of passive ground camouflage target recognition.

articleTitle: High efficient signal processing system for airborne landing aided radar
abstract: This paper first introduces the difficulty of gaining high azimuth resolution of Airborne Landing Aided Radar. Then presents a real-time radar system with different types of board integrated by several FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) and DSP (Digital Signal Processer) to improve the azimuth resolution for Airborne Landing Aided Radar, also provides an ameliorative method for improving azimuth resolution in a real-time system. Finally the experiment demonstrates this system's real-time performance working for de-convolution. It can give the real-time image for Airborne Landing Aided Radar.

articleTitle: Design of Ka-band practical waveguide duplexer
abstract: A brief and practical Ka-band compact waveguide duplexer is demonstrated. A new Structure Y junction is designed that can be expand for others duplexer. U-wave and HFSS three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation are used to Co-simulation. The insertion loss in the transmit path was less than 0.5dB. Final simulation results agreed well with the measured results certified to practicability and accuracy of duplexer.

articleTitle: Cramer-Rao bound of the estimation of direction of arrival for low angle targets
abstract: In low angle tracking scenario, the performance of the direction of arrival (DOA) estimator is not stable. In this paper, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) for low angle tracking is derived to account for this phenomenon. The receiving signal in low angle scenario is modeled as two coherent sources and the effect of the reflection coefficient on the CRB is mainly discussed. In the simulation section, numerical simulations are conducted to study the property of CRB, which indicates that the change of the phase of the reflection coefficient is the main reason why the CRB and the performance of DOA estimators fluctuate.

articleTitle: Clutter suppression and moving target indication with airborne wide-area surveillance radar
abstract: An accurate description of the ground clutter amplitude and power spectral probability density function is important for robust target detection. One goal of this paper is to present a common distribution which matches the Ku-band data sets obtained from GMTI mode. Then a mDT-STAP method was used to suppress clutter, which, in fact, has better performance to detect moving targets. After clutter suppression, the CFAR approach was used to detect moving targets. The data used in this paper is the real data in GMTI mode by an airborne search radar. By utilizing the radar echo data of airborne radar, the location and velocity of the moving targets, can be achieved.

articleTitle: High-precision ranging for radar micro-motion target based on envelope migration
abstract: Phase-Derived-Range, a radar range method based on echo phases, is highly evaluated for its root-mean-square (rms) error within half of wavelength and great used on highly precision ranging for micro-motion target. There are two technical challenges, which are ambiguous Doppler phase acquisition and ambiguity resolution. A method based on envelope migration is proposed in this paper. Firstly, ambiguous phase was extracted from the 1-D range profile; secondly, the ambiguity was resolved by the envelope migration; then, the velocity was estimated by least squares method and the high-precision range was acquired by compensating the error term. In this method, the phase error caused by velocity is compensated at last instead of the ambiguous phase, so that the velocity error does not affect the correctness of ambiguity resolution. Therefore, this method enhances the applicability of this algorithm. The limitations have been provided. Simulation and experiment results validate the performance of the method.

articleTitle: Multi-receiver deception jamming against synthetic aperture radar
abstract: In practical situation, it is difficult to obtain precise electronic surveillance for the non-cooperative targets. Thus the deception modulation which lies deeply on the electronic surveillance would be easy to be identified. In the purpose to modify the parameters dependence, this paper proposes a new deception jamming algorithm based on the cooperation of multi-receivers. This scheme utilizes three receivers to receive the radar signal and one jammer to retransmit the intercepted signal after modulate. In this way, the deception jamming algorithm can work effectively even with inaccurate electronic surveillance parameters. Finally, experimental results of simulated data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: P-band ultra wideband circular synthetic aperture radar experiment and imaging
abstract: Low frequency ultra wideband (UWB) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has shown a great potential when vehicle-size objects are obscured in foliage. The studies imply an aperture angle of at least 180° to include the strongest (broadside) response when the target orientations are unknown. However, the aperture angle of the linear SAR (LSAR) is limited. By using circular traces, the aperture angle of the radar data acquisition has been increased, and the detection capabilities could be improved. An airborne circular SAR (CSAR) data acquisition experiment was carried out in Shaanxi by the National University of Defense Technology (NUDT). The data was acquired by using P-band UWB SAR system along a circular trajectory with the beam spotted on the same area. Compared with LSAR, this imaging mode has a better understanding of the scattering properties of targets, high resolution with low frequency band, and the capability for a 3-D target reconstruction. In this paper, the airborne multiple orbit CSAR data acquisition experiment and the processing of such data are presented.

articleTitle: DOA estimation exploiting unified coprime array with multi-period subarrays
abstract: In this paper, we propose a unified coprime array by extending two subarrays in it from one-period to multi-period. One subarray can have arbitrary number of periods and the other has more periods than it. Therefore, more than one element of the unified structure coincide. The resulting configuration treats the nested array as well as the existing coprime structure, such as the extended one and CACIS as its special case. The comparisons of different coprime arrays are provided. The direction-of-arrival estimation performance and the coarray structures of these coprime arrays are examined through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Experimental array signal processing demonstration system by utilizing microphone array
abstract: Adaptive array signal processing is widely used in radar, communication, sonar, navigation and other signal processing applications. Practical experimental verification is important to evaluate the performance of array signal processing methods. However, the conventional experimental verification for adaptive array signal processing are often conducted with massive radio frequency equipments, which leads to high cost and huge complexity. Therefore, it is necessary to construct an experimental demonstration system with low cost and high flexibility, which can conveniently verify the performance of adaptive array signal processing methods. In this paper, an experimental adaptive array signal processing demonstration system by utilizing the microphone array is proposed, and corresponding experiments of DOA estimation and adaptive beamforming are conducted based on the proposed microphone array system in different environment. Compared with traditional radio frequency system, it is found that the designed system can reduce the experimental cost and complexity of adaptive array signal processing verification.

articleTitle: Echoic flow for target following and approach
abstract: Flow fields naturally measure the time to contact (TTC) between two objects and are symbolized by the parameter "tau". Hence, the term echoic flow represents the use of flow fields in active sensing systems like, radar and sonar. In this paper, we examine the use of the time derivate of the echoic flow parameter "tau dot" in cognitive radar for target following and approach control applications. After a brief introduction of the echoic flow concept and its derivative, three target movement scenarios-stationary target, target moving slower than radar platform and target moving faster than radar platform-are analyzed using both simulations and experiments. The effect of range and range rate measurement accuracy on echoic flow is discussed and methods to achieve suitable levels of accuracy presented.

articleTitle: Extended target detection amid clutter suppression using the combination of the sparsity and total variation
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing of radar range resolution, the extended target echo usually occupies several range cells, and the area of each range cell decreases obviously. Therefore, the traditional detection theory based on point-target and large-area clutter is no longer applicable. A new method based on the local sparsity constraint and total variation technique is presented in this paper. The proposed method takes advantage of interference covariance information to suppress clutter and improve the detection probability. Real radar oceanic surveillance data is applied to illustrate the effectiveness of our method. Results show that the proposed approach outperforms the current compressed sensing techniques and the fully sampled, nonadaptive matched filter in detecting extended targets in the presence of strong clutter.

articleTitle: A novel adaptive filter for highly maneuvering target
abstract: This paper considers the highly maneuvering target tracking as a discrete-time stochastic system with generalized unknown disturbance input, which can represent an arbitrary linear combination of dynamic, random, and deterministic disturbance inputs. The proposed filter based on upper bound filter (UBF) can adaptively optimize adjust factor to find the globally optimal solution of covariance matrices of the state predictions, innovation and estimates. To reduce the linearization error, a iterative optimization frame is designed. The experiment on "S maneuver" of anti-ship missile shows that the proposed filter can significantly reduce the peak estimation errors due to maneuvers.

articleTitle: A compensation method using focusing matrix based on maximum likelihood estimation
abstract: In view of the poor performance of space-time adaptive processing(STAP) when clutter is range-dependent, the paper presents a compensation method using focusing matrix based on maximum likelihood estimation. Firstly, clutter amplitude is estimated utilizing maximum likelihood estimation, and clutter patches with greater amplitude are selected. Secondly, focusing matrix is evaluated by space-time steering vector of clutter patches, and a linear transformation is directly implemented on the training data using the focusing matrix. Thirdly, clutter-plus-noise covariance matrix(CCM) of the cell under text(CUT) is estimated utilizing the transformed data and thus the self-adaptive weights are evaluated. The proposed method, in which non-uniform sampling is adopted, performs better compared with classical focusing matrix method. Lastly, the simulation tests its validity.

articleTitle: Coordinate descent for cognitve radar adaptation
abstract: By monitoring surroundings and adapting system parameters, cognitive radar has been shown to outperform traditional feed-forward radar systems. This paper builds upon the fully adaptive radar (FAR) framework for cognition. A coordinate descent (CD) algorithm is used with the FAR framework to adapt two radar parameters while tracking a single target. Simulated and experimental results are used to demonstrate how CD outperforms the sequential optimizations previously used with the FAR framework. Additional optimizations not previously used with the FAR framework are included for further comparisons.

articleTitle: Coprime sampling with deterministic digital filters in compressive sensing radar
abstract: Compressive Sensing radar has been studied in the past few years, however, some difficulties still need to be solved both in theory and engineering. For the difficulty in designing random measurement matrix on the hardware, a scheme of co-prime sampling with deterministic filters in compressive sensing radar is proposed. A deterministic low-pass filter is used to replace the random filter in order to facilitate the implementation of the hardware system. The extraction from the convolution result of the received signal and the filter is equivalent to the process of measurement. Extraction functions with co-prime extraction factors are employed to decide the structure of measurement matrix and the compression factor. The numerical results indicate that the scheme of co-prime sampling with deterministic filters can realize accurate reconstruction of sparse targets scene by considerable fewer samples in radar system.

articleTitle: Vessel target tracking exploiting frequency diversity for dual-frequency HFSWR
abstract: Due to the effect of the first-order sea clutter, some targets with certain radial velocities cannot be detected by a single frequency High Frequency Surface Wave Radar (HFSWR). These missed contacts will result in track fragmentation. In this paper, a vessel target tracking method exploiting frequency diversity is proposed for dual-frequency HFSWR. Taking one frequency as the main frequency for tracking and the other as the auxiliary one, when a target goes into the blind velocity zone of the main frequency, the detected points by the auxiliary frequency are employed for the following tracking process. Tracking experiments were conducted on real data with synchronous AIS track as comparison, the results verify that the proposed method can repair some fractured tracks caused by blind velocity with boosted capability for track persistency and accuracy; meanwhile, the real-time character of track output can be guaranteed.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation of rectilinear signals using multiple noncollocated and diversely polarized antennas
abstract: A root manifold decoupling method is proposed for the estimation of direction-of-arrival (DOA) and noncircularity coefficient of rectilinear signals (also known as second order fully noncircular signals, such as AM and BPSK signals) by using a uniform linear array of multiple noncollocated and diversely polarized antennas. Incorporated with eigendecomposition and the noncircular cum polarimetric rank reduction technique, the differences of signals in space, polarization, and noncircularity are jointly exploited in a closed-form widely linear framework, leading to an enhanced parameter estimation accuracy. Simulation results are included to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Waveform optimization in through-the-wall imaging for ghost mitigation
abstract: The ghost clutter deteriorates target detection in through-the-wall imaging and is difficult to remove without the building structure information. In order to enhance the performance of ghost mitigation, a novel waveform optimization method is put forward in this paper to improve the signal to clutter ratio (SCR). Experiments on practical echo data further illustrate the improvement of SCR while keeping the imaging quality with the application of proposed waveform optimization.

articleTitle: Research on technology of microwave-photonic-based multifunctional radar
abstract: Prospective characteristics of the next generation of radar is investigated in this paper, combined with future requirement. The demands of the next generation radar for the wide band, high speed, parallelism and high integration are precisely the four prominent respects of photonics. The technological path of future radar could hopefully be interdisciplinary fusion to solve bottleneck problems in the microwave field by means of optical methods, ideas and technical features, namely constructing microwave photonics technology based radar system. One system architecture of multifunctional radar based on the technology of microwave photonics is proposed. Meanwhile, representative techniques such as photonic frequency conversion and photonic beamforming are presented. Some stages of experiment and test results are reported.

articleTitle: Generalized iterative adaptive approach for spectrum estimation based on variational Bayesian inference
abstract: Iterative adaptive approach (IAA) which attracted significant interest as a sparse learning method in recent years has find many applications such as spectrum estimation, source location, MIMO imaging and wideband detection, etc. However, the applications of IAA in practice typically require discretizing continuous parameter space by grid to form the sparse representation basis, which is not only the source of heavy computation burden for large problems, but also degrades the accuracy of estimation and restricts the sparsity that could be achieved. It was demonstrated in this paper that IAA could be derived as a special case of the well known Variational Bayesian Inference algorithm under appropriate probabilistic model and assumptions. In addition, a generalized IAA method was proposed to deal with continuous parameters and eliminate the necessity of discretization, which achieve better estimation accuracy and sparsity as shown in numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Identification-while-scanning of MAF for narrowband radar via hierarchical basis pursuit
abstract: This paper proposes a novel identification-while-scanning (IWS) method for a multi-aircraft formation of narrowband radar. First, a multiple chirp signal model is established for MAF in a single scan, where different aircrafts can have different Doppler centers and Doppler rates. It is clear that the short dwell time in IWS may significantly limit the discrimination ability of different chirp components. Based on the sparsity of MAF in the Doppler parameter space, a novel hierarchical basis pursuit (HBP) method is proposed to obtain high sparse recovery performance as well as computational efficiency. It is shown that an MAF can be effectively identified via HBP by using only about one hundred microsecond echoes to meet the IWS applications. Finally, some numerical experiment results are provided based on simulated and real measured data to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Regularized polarimetric target detection in the presence of inhomogeneous and/or non-stationary clutter
abstract: The polarimetric information of radar targets can be exploited to improve the detection performance, especially when the spatial-Doppler processing is insufficient. In the case of inhomogeneous and/or non-stationary clutters, however, the potential of the polarimetric detector is restricted due to the limited training data size, particularly when the sample support is less than the number of array elements. This paper presents an iterative shrinkage based regularized polarimetric target detection scheme to deal with the mentioned under-sampling problem in the presence of either Gaussian or compound Gaussian clutters. The involved shrinkage parameter in the convex combined sample covariance matrix or fixed-point covariance matrix is herein adaptively determined by using a newly developed neighbor point matching technique. Performance assessment using synthetic and real data shows that the proposed detector outperforms the non-regularized counterpart in terms of the probability of detection.

articleTitle: Auto-focusing compressed sensing algorithm for through-the-wall imaging
abstract: In this paper, the auto-focusing compressed sensing (ACS) algorithm is proposed to retrieve behind-the-wall image with unknown wall parameters. The ACS algorithm proposed updates the measurement matrix and constructs the behind-the-wall image alternately within an iterative framework. The nonlinear conjugate gradient method is used to estimate the wall parameters, where the gradient functions in analytical form are derived based on the generalized electromagnetic wave penetrating propagation model for through-the-wall radars. Real data are used to validate the proposed method. It is shown that the proposed method can yield finer resolution with less data as compared with the conventional through-the-wall imaging method, e.g. back-projection penetrating imaging method.

articleTitle: Super-resolution processing for shipborne HFSWR based on an improved IMP
abstract: In this paper, Incremental Multi-Parameter (IMP) Algorithm, a kind of approximate maximum likelihood method which can realize super-resolution, is applied into shipborne HFSWR for angular resolution. In order to meet the need of single snapshot processing and practical application with IMP, an improved IMP algorithm is proposed, based on single snapshot covariance matrix estimation and beam-space processing. In this improved algorithm, single snapshot covariance matrix and beam-space processing contributes to a more accurate matrix, whose dimension has been reduced, and beam-space processing contributes for a flatter SNNR. Compared with the traditional IMP for single snapshot data, the computer simulation and real data processing results show effectiveness of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of broadband high-transmission frequency selective surface structure with micro-elements modulation
abstract: This paper proposed a new frequency selective surface (FSS) structure with micro-elements modulation for radome design based on the scanning independence of slot array in the theoretical analysis. This new type of FSS structure puts the micro-elements on both sides of double-layer hexagon slot arrays FSS for modulation to realize broadband high-transmission and to reduce radar cross section (RCS) of antennas. Simulated and measured results indicate that the proposed FSS structure can provide stable broadband high-transmission frequency responses for both horizontal (TM) and vertical (TE) polarization under incident angles from 0 to 60 degree.

articleTitle: High resolution range profile reconstruction based on local reoptimization FOCUSS algorithm
abstract: The Focal Underdetermined System Solver (FOCUSS) method is widely applied in the compressive sensing (CS) based high resolution range profile (HRRP) reconstruction. However, the parameter estimation of the scattering center type is not accurate enough. In this paper, an algorithm named by local reoptimization FOCUSS is presented to deal with such a case. After the traditional FOCUSS algorithm being applied, the estimated parameters of each extracted scattering center in a given range cell are modified by minimizing the construction residual upon each atom with different type of parameter. Finally, the numerical simulations show that the proposed method can effectively estimate the parameters of attributed scattering centers while the traditional FOCUSS algorithm fails, especially for the estimation of type parameter.

articleTitle: Joint sparse modeling for multi-pulse distributed MIMO radar
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) theory has been applied to distributed MIMO radar systems in recent years, constituting space diversity by receiving echo from different angles. In this paper, we validate a joint sparse representation model of the received signal assemble, and further extend the single pulse distributed MIMO radar signal to multiple pulses. Three difference kinds of joint sparse model is studied in this paper and we make a comparison of them to choose the optimal one. Simulation results demonstrate that employing the proposed joint sparse representation model, distributed CS MIMO radar can detect target's parameters accurately.

articleTitle: The effect of toughening agents on heat-resistance, mechanical and dielectric properties of epoxy resins used in radome materials
abstract: This paper discussed the effects of different toughening agents on heat resistance, mechanical properties, dielectric properties and moisture absorption properties of E-51/Dicy systems used in radome materials. Based on DSC results, we discussed the reactivity and heat resistance of the four systems. The bending properties and impact strength were tested to reveal the toughness of the resins. The dielectric properties and moisture absorption were also evaluated. The results revealed all the three toughening agents could increase the impact properties and decrease the dielectric constant, meanwhile moisture absorption was lower than the untreated sample. JER 1256 and PEK-C had more obvious effects on toughness and could also keep the heat resistance. The result of E-20 system showed the lowest ε and tgδ.

articleTitle: A novel approach to mpsk modulation recognition through compressive signal processing strategy
abstract: The theory of compressive sensing (CS) enables the recovery of sparse or approximately sparse signal from a significantly small set of measurements. This progress has inspired a new idea that many signal processing problems can be solved based on the framework of CS. In this work, we employ CS in the task of inferring the modulation of a communication signal without full signal recovery which is the usual focus in previous literatures. We show that the differences in the higher order power spectrum between MPSK signals can be used as the features for automatic modulation recognition (AMR). Subsequently, we present the sparsity of these features in the Fourier domain and provide an approach to extract features from nonuniform compressive samples of observed signals. The proposed method is validated by simulation experiments through the support vector machine (SVM).

articleTitle: OTHR transient interference suppression based on the relaxed PCP
abstract: The performance of high-frequency sky-wave over-the-horizon radar is affected by transient interference. Traditional methods used to suppress the transient interference in several steps. First, the position of the transient interference is localized in the time domain, and then the corrupted time samples are set to zero. Finally, the partial data are reconstructed by interpolation. However, the performance of the target detection would be significantly decreased if the interference corrupts a significant portion of the received signal. This paper presents a novel approach for suppressing the transient interference based on the relaxed principal component pursuit (PCP). Using a Hankel structured matrix constructed by the received signal in a given range cell, the transient interference in the Hankel matrix shows sparse property and the remainder signal shows low rank. Then the transient interference excision could be solved by the Relaxed PCP. Without transient interference location and data interpolation, the proposed method can remove the transient interference, and it is also helpful for improving the signal to noise ratio (SNR). The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Spatial temporal adaptive processing based on delay vector tracking loop
abstract: In order to overcome the high complexity, the slow convergence speed and the week robustness of the Spatial Temporal Adaptive Processing (STAP). In this letter, a novel robust scheme combining a variable forgetting factor mechanism STAP algorithm and vector delay lock loop (VDLL) is proposed to improve the anti-jamming capability of the navigation receiver. The VDLL is used to supply reference information relying on the unique structure of the coarse acquisition code for spatial temporal adaptive processing. Then an improved variable forgetting factor constant modulus recursive least squares algorithm (ITVFF-CCM-RLS) is proposed for enhancing satellite signals and suppressing interferences. Finally, the navigation signal without interference is used for VDLL tracking and calculating satellite pseudoranges. Simulation results show that the improved method can not only effectively improve the convergence speed, but also ensure the reliability of the receiver in the presence of intense interference.

articleTitle: Inter-range-cell interference free compression algorithm: Performance in operational conditions
abstract: The analysis of the performance of a novel algorithm found in the literature, the inter-range cell interference (IRCI) free compression algorithm, is presented in this paper. The algorithm presents a Dirac response in distance compression with a pedestal error at −350 dB. These performances would be very valuable for the radar field. The robustness of the performances for the IRCI free compression algorithm and matched filtering (MF) compression algorithm are explored first in simulations with point targets. Their sensitivity to bit resolution is also assessed. Both algorithms are then tested with measured signals from a wireless test performed using an ultra-wide band software defined radar platform with 800 MHz instantaneous bandwidth in X-band on a trihedral corner reflector. For an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing signal with N carriers, the results show that IRCi free compression algorithm offers an extra 2 dB in contrast for this measurement with an added processing cost of at least 4N real multiplications when compared to MF compression algorithm.

articleTitle: Data association algorithm for ballistic missile target based on optimal assignment strategy
abstract: During the penetration of ballistic missile targets, there are lots of baits or decoys forming group targets. Targets in the same group are so close to each other that it's difficult to track each target continuously and correctly without false data association. False data association leads to false target recognition and orbit computation, which will shorten time to intercept the ballistic missile. A data association algorithm based on optimal assignment strategy (OASDA) is proposed. First, consider the data association problem as a special case of optimal assignment problem. Then build probability assignment matrix based on normalized residuals, speed, heading, AD and other characteristic parameters. Finally solve the assignment matrix to get measure and track pairs. Simulation results show that the OASDA algorithm can significantly improve the accuracy of data association within the same target group.

articleTitle: Change detection of foliage concealed vehicles via visual attention
abstract: Traditional statistically-based change detection of foliage-concealed targets is usually limited by pixels' intensities which differ from each other in the multi-temporal UWB SAR image pair. To solve this problem, we propose a method of change detection based on a modified bottom-up visual attention model (VAM). In this method, multi-scale spatial features of an image are achieved by using the Gaussian pyramid analysis and combined into one visual saliency map by processing the center-surrounding difference maps. Then, the morphology theory and spatial characteristics of vehicles are exploited to detect salient locations in the saliency map. In the end, the salient locations between two saliency maps of the image pair are compared one by one and change detection of targets is acquired. Simulation results show that not only the probability of detection of foliage-concealed vehicle targets is raised, but the computational speed is able to be improved as well.

articleTitle: A parallel implementation of RFT on GPU
abstract: Radon Fourier Transform (RFT) is a kind of generalized MTD, which can integrate along the track of targets. However, it is not easy for RFT to be engineered due to the calculating burden. Aiming at this problem, a kind of RFT parallelization strategy is put forward based on GPU and CUDA. Through experimental verification, the execution time of RFT on GPU platform proved a great speedup compared with that of RFT and fast RFT on CPU. In addition, it suggests in the results that the execution time can be as fast as MTD when RFT results are saved in global memory.

articleTitle: Superresolution ground mapping for scanning radar with IAA-based inverse filtering
abstract: The spatial resolution of scanning radar in azimuth is constrained by the antenna beam width. Several superresolution approaches have been applied to scanning radars to enhance the azimuth resolution, but they suffer from limited resolution improvement. In this paper, a superresolution approach is performed by truncating the spectrum of which only low frequencies are reserved. In this way, the ill-posed problem of direct deconvolution can be solved, but the spectrum truncation will aggravate the smooth effect. To solve this problem, we propose an inverse filtering based on iterative adaptive approach (IAA) to suppress sidelobes and obtain a higher resolution. Numerical results illustrate the superior performance of the proposed IAA-based inverse Filtering over the existing superresolution methods.

articleTitle: Blind classification of multiple frequency-hopping signals using TOA sequence
abstract: This paper proposes a blind classification method for multiple frequency hopping (FH) signals based on time of arrival (TOA) sequence, without the knowledge of FH pattern and needing only a single channel receiver. The method obtains the residue TOA sequence by plane transform, eliminates outliers values using erosion algorithm and classifies the pulses finally using k-means clustering algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed method is effective and achieves a good classification performance based on single channel receiver.

articleTitle: An iterative matching space-time adaptive processing for airborne measured data
abstract: In this paper, we consider an effective iterative matching space-time adaptive processing (STAP) method for ground clutter suppression in airborne radar from the viewpoint of steering vector perturbation. To achieve the optimum matching of the unknown actual steering vector, a practical search strategy of actual spatial steering vector is established and the corresponding method of spatial angle measure is also discussed. Finally, airborne measured datasets are used as examples to assess the performance of the proposed algorithm and make comparisons with the traditional pulse Doppler (PD) processing.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive beamforming using Doppler property restoral
abstract: Diagonal loading (DL) is the most widely used method to improve the robustness of the Capon beamformer in the presence of finite sample effect and/or signal-of-interest (SOI) steering vector mismatch. However, the determination of the optimal DL level is a challenging task. A Doppler property restoral based method is herein proposed for selecting an appropriate DL level to extract a Doppler SOI buried in interferences plus ambient noise. Simulation results are included to illustrate the performance of the proposed user-parameter-free beamformer.

articleTitle: Numerical study of microjet array impingement cooling device with micro channels
abstract: An innovative microjet array impingement cooling device with micro channels is proposed to cope with the demanding thermal management issue imposed by phased array radar high-density RF devices. Numerical simulation was conducted to the jet impingement cooling devices with commercial CFD code ANSYS Icepak. The influences of microjet flow inlet temperature, RF package substrates thermal conductivities to the heat dissipation effect of this device were investigated. The results indicated that when micro channels were introduced to the jet impingement cooling device, the heat dissipation effect was strengthened obviously. The maximum temperature of the RF device increases as the increasing of the microjet fluid inlet temperature. The thermal conductivities of the substrates also had significant impact to the heat dissipation effect of the device. While the temperature increment of the jet flow had little relationship with its inlet temperature.

articleTitle: Radar power control method based on IMM-IF in LPI radar network
abstract: In order to achieve the important tactical requirement of low probability of intercept (LPI) in the radar network, dynamically controlling the emission of the radars is very necessary. Firstly, a data fusion method based on an interacting multiple model and information filtering (IMM-IF) algorithm is presented. Then, the influence of the emitted power is considered in the tracking performance of the radar network, and a novel power scheduling method based IMM-IF is proposed, which controls the power of radar according to predicted covariance matrix during tracking. Finally, taking advantage of the relation model between the emitted power and the tracking performance, the Wind Driven Optimization (WDO) method is used to select the emitted power of the radar network. The tracking accuracy and LPI performance are demonstrated in the Monte Carlo simulations. The results are validated through the comparison with other methods.

articleTitle: Multiple targets tracking in radar system based on cross sector probability hypothesis density filter
abstract: Problems and solutions are discussed for the application of the Probability Hypothesis Density (PHD) filter in radar system. The results for engineering applications of the multiple target tracking based on PHD filtering in radar system are introduced. Results showed that the PHD filter can effectively solve the problems of Track initiation, organizing batch, and so on,.

articleTitle: A precise and compact height of burst sensor for guided missiles
abstract: Height of Burst (HOB) sensor is one of the critical parts in guided missiles. While seekers control the guiding scheme of the missile, proximity sensors set the trigger for increased effectiveness of the warhead. For the well-developed guided missiles of Roketsan, a novel proximity sensor is developed. The design of the sensor is for multi-purpose use. In this presentation, the application of the sensor is explained for operation as a HOB sensor in the range of 3m-50m with ± 1m accuracy. Measurement results are also presented. The same sensor is currently being developed for proximity sensor for missile defence.

articleTitle: The calculation algorithm for average wind speed and direction in prediction technology of OTH radar detection range
abstract: Radar may realize b-Los detection when electromagnetic wave propagation trapped in evaporation duct. When predicting the OTH radar detection range, the parameter of atmospheric wind speed and direction are badly needed in the processes of calculating atmospheric refractivity profile and the loss of electromagnetic propagation. P-J model is used to study the effect of wind speed to evaporation duct height. Parabolic equation is used to study the effect of wind speed to loss of electromagnetic propagation under the condition of evaporation duct atmosphere. Three algorithm including scalar, unit vector and vector are introduced and are compared in prediction of radar detection range by experiment on the sea. The result shows that average wind speed and direction calculated by unit vector has a better result than the others in predicting radar detection range.

articleTitle: Bistatic ISAR imaging under low SNR via fast complex approximate message passing
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) has attracted much interest since it can be used to improve inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging. The complexity and robustness of imaging algorithm are two important aspects in CS-based ISAR imaging. In this paper, a fast complex approximate message passing (FCAMP) is presented to overcome strong noise and high-complexity for high resolution bistatic ISAR (B-ISAR) imaging. Approximate message passing (AMP) is extended to the complex field for realizing complex reconstruction in B-ISAR imaging. The calculation of matrix-vector multiplication is reduced from O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) to O(N logN) operations by fast Fourier transform. Simulated data are used to test the robustness and the speediness of the bistatic ISAR imaging framework with proposed FCAMP algorithm compared with other current methods. Experimental results show that the proposed approach is capable of effective suppression of noise and fast reconstruction of precise scattering centers.

articleTitle: Sparse array design for distributed aperture coherence-synthetic radar
abstract: This paper considers the sparse linear array (SLA) design problem of coherent unambiguous transmit for the distributed aperture coherence-synthetic radar (DACR), accounting for the antenna size constraint and geography constraint in which elements can not be placed in a given aperture. We develop the peak sidelobe level (PSL) based cost function, which considers the sum of the PSL when the mainlobe located at all scanning angles. Then, we derive the antenna element locations by minimizing the cost function through PSO algorithm. Finally, several numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed SLA design method.

articleTitle: Urban land use information extraction using ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 data based on object-oriented method
abstract: Both spatial texture details and polarization characterizations are contained in high resolution polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) data, which makes it possible to extract the land use information of urban areas. The object-oriented method has been proposed as a tool to process and analyze the high resolution PolSAR data. In this paper, a resolution-preserving PolSAR denoising method was used to preprocess the ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 data. Then a multi-scale segmentation technique based on spectral clustering was used to segment the preprocessed data. Finally, the buildings, roads, green space, and bare soil were extracted using the object-oriented method from the ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 data in some urban areas of Chengdu. Experiment results indicate that the oriented-objected method is effective for extracting the land use information of urban areas.

articleTitle: Study on PRF design and Doppler measurement in spaceborne cloud profiling radar
abstract: This paper studies PRF design and Doppler measurement in spaceborne cloud profiling radar (CPR). The relationship between PRF and Doppler velocity accuracy is considered. The operational PRF will be constrained by CPR's geometry and timing parameters. The constraint relationship between PRF and the radar parameters are given. The available PRF for typical situation is simulated considering the distance constraints. Antenna sidelobes ambiguity and range ambiguity are also analyzed, and insults show that these two limitations can be ignored for spaceborne CPR. Derivation of velocity accuracy is shown based on Zrnic's method. And simulations for two different modes of operations are obtained using the derivation result.

articleTitle: A space-polarization collaborative algorithm for HFSWR
abstract: For the high frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR), the presence of ionospheric clutter seriously degrades its capability of receiving target echoes. Thus various ionospheric clutter mitigation methods are investigated based on space domain. However, the gains of antennas in vertical incidence can lead to channel amplitude inconsistency, which can degrade the performances of aforementioned space-domain-based methods. To solve this problem, a polarimetric-adaptive-based space-polarization collaborative algorithm (PAB-SPCA) is proposed by exploiting polarization domain, and enhances performance of ionospheric clutter suppression in the space-polarization domain. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is effective for channel amplitude consistency and provides superior suppression performance.

articleTitle: Sidelobe reduction in stepped-frequency-continuous-wave MIMO TWRI of moving targets
abstract: Due to the improper time-division multiplexed (TDM) mode, a undesirable sidelobe occurs if the target moves a little fast while a stepped-frequency-continuous-wave (SFCW) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) through-wall radar (TWR) is used to monitor moving targets by real-time imaging. In this paper, we firstly derive the formulas of range shift and pulse spreading due to the target motion, and then we change the TDM mode from switching the transmitting antenna at the end of complete SFCW periods to switching at every frequency, which is very conducive to eliminating the undesirable sidelobe. This modification makes the tracking of higher speed human target possible at a low pulse repetition frequency (PRF).

articleTitle: An improved autofocus approach based on 2-D inverse filtering for airborne spotlight SAR
abstract: For airborne spotlight mode synthetic aperture radar (SAR) autofocusing, the residual range cell migration (RRCM) results in performance degradation. An improved inverse filtering (IF) autofocus approach based on the isolated strong point target is proposed in this paper. The new approach can simultaneously compensate both azimuth phase error and the two dimensional coupling phase error caused by the residual range migration. Therefor the bad effect caused by RRCM on autofocusing is eliminated, and the performance of inverse filtering autofocus algorithm is improved obviously. The results of real-measured data processing validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-frequency dual-circularly-polarized vivaldi antenna array
abstract: A dual-frequency dual-circularly-polarized vivaldi antenna array is proposed in this paper. The array element is constructed by crossing two vivaldi antenna. To realize function of the circular polarization, the array element is fed by a 3dB bridge. The best structure parameters are fond by using Genetic Algorithm (GA). Simulation results of impedance and axial ratio show that array can work in dual-frequency band. Based on these properties, the proposed antenna array has great benefit to the design and performance analysis of dual-frequency circularly-polarized phased array antenna.

articleTitle: Study on search performance of long range early-warning phased array radar
abstract: Search ability of long range early-warning phased array radar without indication information is studied in this paper, based on the background of near space hypersonic targets defense. Design principle and validation method of radar search parameters such as search screen, signal cycle and search frame period are deeply discussed in the case of near space work pattern, the shortest cross-screen distance and the minimum number of scans of radar are formulated based on the target motion state. Finally, radar detecting ability is analyzed through simulation, which shows that radar has the whole capacity to capture the target when it coming right against the face, while it should take the mode of TWS when it coming from behind the head space.

articleTitle: Detection of low-observable maneuvering target using high-order generalized Lv's distribution
abstract: Long-time integration is an effective way to strengthen the weak signal from low-observable target. However, the performances are affected by the range and Doppler migrations during the long observation time. In this paper, Doppler characteristics of a maneuvering target with high-order motion are studied and a novel transform, i.e., high-order generalized Lv's distribution (HGLVD), is proposed to realize the long-time coherent integration. The HGLVD can accurately and directly represent the m-D signal in the chirp rate and chirp change (CRCC) domain appearing as an obvious peak. The proposed method is simple for not introducing any nonphysical attributes such as transform angle or order. Experiment with CSIR radar data indicates that the proposed method can achieve higher integration gain and better clutter suppression ability.

articleTitle: OFDLFM waveform based mixed integration for supersonic target detection
abstract: This paper introduced the wide-band OFDLFM waveform to improve the supersonic target detection performance in the deception jamming environment. Given the waveform model, a mixed integration technique, which combines both coherent integration in the same channels and multi-channel fusion among different channels, is introduced to enhance integration gain and overcome different kinds of deception jamming. At last, the numerical experiments results prove its effectiveness.

articleTitle: SAR image change detection based on nonstationary analysis and conditional random fields
abstract: In this paper, we propose a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image change detection algorithm based on SAR image nonstationary analysis and conditional random field (CRF) model. This algorithm segments the SAR images into two nonstationary regions with the Triplet Markov Field (TMF) model which incorporates a U field to describe the images' nonstationary nature. The combined posterior probability of the CRF model consists of two parts: the unary potential and the pairwise potential. The unary potential is modeled by support vector machine (SVM) using the texture features extracted from the two-temporal SAR images, and the pairwise potential is constructed by the multilevel logistical model to capture the spatial interactions of the log-ratio image. Both the unary and pairwise potentials are improved with the introduction of the U field. The parameters of the pairwise potential are estimated by the iterative conditional estimation (ICE) algorithm. The iterative conditional model (ICM) algorithm is utilized for updating the combined posterior probability, and the final change detection results are obtained when it converges. Finally, experimental results on four two-temporal SAR images validate the effectiveness of the proposed image change detection algorithm.

articleTitle: A method used for InISAR interferometric phase unwrapping
abstract: Interferometric ISAR can obtain 3D image of the target. The location of the target can be obtained from the interferometric phase. Phase unwrapping is a key procedure in InISAR signal processing, as the interferometric phase may be ambiguous. In this paper, we propose a method used for InISAR interferometric phase unwrapping. This method uses dual frequency conjugated processing (DFCP) to perform phase unwrapping. This method is equivalent to increasing the carrier wave length and can expand the measurement range of the cross direction. After DFPC we can obtain an unwrapped interferometric phase. It can be used as the reference phase in the following phase unwrapping procedure. Simulation data is used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: The general thought of mobile design for large movable radar
abstract: Movable radar needs to transfer from place to place and operates quickly at the new working position, Large number of equipment makes mobility quota difficult to achieve. In this paper, the general thought of mobile design is discussed and is applied in a design of a radar which mobile quota is just 1 hour with about 250 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of antenna, the weight of 50,000 kg of all equipment. Mobile design on antenna unit is focused on. The most important aspects relatively are transportation design, vehicle design, erecting or teardown design of antenna, antenna design including separating or connecting design of antenna. This paper shows mobility quota has been achieved in the example above.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive beamforming with joint robustness against convariance uncertainty and steering vector mismatch
abstract: We address a new adaptive beamforming algorithm with joint robustness against both covariance matrix uncertainty and steering vector (SV) mismatch, which needs neither the norm of the SV nor its error upper bound. Firstly, we propose a modified general linear combination (MGLC) algorithm to obtain a better estimation of covariance matrix. Then using the MGLC-based estimation, we formulate a quadratic convex optimization problem in view of the Capon power spectrum to obtain a refined SV. The proposed algorithm maximizes the beamformer output power under two constraints that the mismatch vector is orthogonal to the presumed SV and the refined SV does not converge to any interference SV. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed beamformer outperforms the beamformers which only have robustness against single one of these two kinds of array mismatches.

articleTitle: Waveform design for extended target detection under a peak to average power ratio constraint
abstract: This paper investigates optimal waveform design for extended target detection under the constraint of constant modulus. Firstly, the probability of detection as a function of the waveform is established. Then, considering the optimization of detection waveform for extended target under the constraint of constant modulus is a concave problem, the paper proposes a method to transform the concave optimization problem to a convex optimization problem by converting the constant modulus constraint to peak to average power ratio (PAR) constraint. Finally, detection performance of the derived waveform is analyzed for a typical extended target model.

articleTitle: Detection of unresolved targets for plane array radar based on monopulse ratio
abstract: Detection of unresolved targets is an important prerequisite to the resolution of unresolved targets. This paper points out the difference of monopulse ratio between a single target and unresolved targets. After approximate analysis of the monopulse ratio distribution, unresolved targets detector for plane array radar is put forward. Numerical experiment results demonstrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of integrative intelligence support system
abstract: In view of the requirement of fault diagnosis and maintenance support of radar equipment, a solution to radar integrative intelligence support system is proposed in this paper. The system is integrated with fault perception, confirmation, maintenance and spare parts management, which realizes fault collection, prognostic, confirmation and interactive maintain in virtue of different sensors, expert system, IETM and so on. By using the interconvert technology of LRU, it diminishes the sorts and the numbers of spare parts, which is different from traditional special spare parts. The system realizes the share of spare parts in different areas in virtue of network, and reduces the cost of spare parts. The sorts and the numbers of spare parts are planed effectively according to the actual situation.

articleTitle: A novel nonreciprocal detector for simultaneous polarimetric radar
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the polarimetric detection algorithms in simultaneous polarimetric radar. The classical polarimetric detection performance of the optimal polarimetric detector (OPD), the polarimetric whitening filter (PWF), the Polarimetric Matched Filter (PMF) and Span Detection are summarized under the reciprocity. However, with consideration of the influence of the spatial polarization characteristics of antenna, a novel nonreciprocal polarimetric detector under nonreciprocity is proposed. Through the detection performance comparison of stable target in Gaussian noise, nonreciprocal algorithm yields better detection performance than OPD.

articleTitle: Adaptive signal detection in partially-known interference and unknown Gaussian noise
abstract: Besides the noise and possible target signal, the data received by radar often contains interference, which can significantly degrade the detection performance. This paper considers the problem of detecting a target in partially-known interference and unknown Gaussian noise. The interference is unknown, but it is constrained in a subspace orthogonal to the signal in the whitened space. According to the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) criterion, we proposed an effective detector, which has improved detection performance than the corresponding Rao and Wald tests. Remarkably, the GLRT in the presence of interference has the same form as that in the absence of interference. However, the interference affects the detection performance of the detector. The effectiveness of the proposed detector is demonstrated by Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Detector of distributed target based on hybrid cubic phase function
abstract: In high resolution radar systems, the return signals can be considered as a multiple linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal with small frequency rate (FR). In this paper, we propose a hybrid cubic phase function (HCPF) to transform a signal from the time domain into the FR domain. The HCPF takes the advantages of the integrated cubic phase function (ICPF) and product cubic phase function (PCPF) in analyzing the LFM signal. Using the HCPF, the return signal is concentrated in a low FR region, while the Gaussian noise spreads over the entire FR region. From this, we further propose a distributed target detector. This detector uses a single return signal and thus has the ability to detect the maneuvering target with a very high velocity. Finally, the proposed detector is evaluated by recorded radar data. Experimental results show that the proposed detector outperforms its competitors.

articleTitle: SCC-MUSIC algorithm for DOA estimation based on cyclostationarity
abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation using single channel. Based on cyclostationarity, the signal model for DOA estimation using single channel is formulated, and the Single Channel Cyclic Multiple Signal Classification (SCC-MUSIC) algorithm is proposed. The cyclic autocorrelation matrix, other than the covariance matrix, is used in the proposed method, which shows a higher resolution limit than the existing single channel MUSIC algorithm because of using signal selective property at cyclic frequency domain. Moreover, the proposed algorithm applies to both the narrowband and wideband sources. Computer simulations have been done and the results are compared with the existing single channel MUSIC algorithm and multi-channel MUSIC algorithm.

articleTitle: A novel off-grid DOA estimation via weighted subspace fitting
abstract: In this paper, a novel off-grid direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm involving sparse recovery is proposed based on weighted subspace fitting, in which multiple snapshots are used and effects of off-grid DOA are taken into account. The DOA estimation problem is formulated as a binary cost function, then an iterative sparse recovery algorithm alternating resolved the unknown variables with weighted linorm approximation method is developed to estimate DOA accurately. The proposed algorithm obtains improved accuracy compared with the existing methods. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can estimate the DOA with high accuracy for correlated signals while maintaining a relatively low computational cost.

articleTitle: Frame segmentation and recognition algorithm for ship's HRRPs based on hypothesis testing
abstract: Radar target recognition for ship target plays an important part in maritime early warning and detection systems. And high resolution range profile (HRRP) is a hot research topic because of its easy measurement, processing and excellent environment adaptability. According to the mechanism of HRRP, the complex gauss statistical characteristic is analyzed using the hypothesis testing. And frame segmentation is realized with the K-S hypothesis testing, which make the each frame data satisfy the same gauss distribution and the different frame data satisfy the different distribution. Finally, the Bayes classifier is presented based the complex gauss distribution for ship recognition and the experiment results validate the effectiveness of the proposed frame segmentation and recognition algorithm.

articleTitle: A fast polar format algorithm based on variable PRF for bistatic SAR
abstract: Polar Format Algorithm (PFA), which is a classic algorithm for bistatic SAR imaging, has important significance in spotlight bistatic SAR system. In this paper, a fast polar format algorithm based on variable PRF for bistatic SAR is proposed. This algorithm can correct range cell migration (RCM) without high-precision interpolation, which can improve the computation efficiency. Point target simulation validates the algorithm.

articleTitle: The chirp-based analog to information conversion in the LFM pulse compression radar
abstract: The analog to information conversion (AIC) via random demodulation (RD) has suffered the performance loss in reducing the sampling rate of linear frequency modulation (LFM) pulse compression radar, especially for the local non-sparse targets in high resolution environment. In this paper, a novel AIC scheme via the determinate chirp mixing sequence is proposed to deal with this problem. The determinate chirp mixing sequence is given in two modes with fixed time duration and fixed bandwidth, respectively. Due to the spread spectrum as well as the local narrowband characteristics in undersampling condition, the determinate chirp mixing sequence guarantees the reconstruction performance of local non-sparse targets with low hardware consumption. Performance analysis and simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of chirp mixing sequence in the restricted isometry property (RIP) and reconstruction performance of non-sparse targets for LFM pulse compression radar.

articleTitle: Weak multitarget detection exploiting CPHD filter for ubiquitous radar
abstract: In order to detect and track the moving weak multitarget through ubiquitous radar observations, this paper proposes a cardinalized probability hypothesis density (CPHD) filter based on sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) implementation. The traditional tracking method, such as joint probabilistic data association (JPDA) algorithm, suffers from computational problem in closely-spaced targets and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environment. The CPHD filter is a multitarget moment approximation of the multitarget Bayes filter with both the detecting and tracking capability. The proposed method is designed for the general weak multitarget detecting scenarios with unknown parameters. In particular, the filter is derived by exploiting the tools of the finite set statistics (FISST) to solve the multisensory-multitarget computational problem of CPHD. Instead of processing in data level, the processing in signal level schemes alleviates the information loss, since the measurements of ubiquitous radar can be in in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) form. Simulation results show that the proposed filter yields stable cardinality and state estimates.

articleTitle: The airborne X-SAR calibration with high resolution
abstract: X-SAR system is the airborne imaging radar with multi-mode synthetic aperture radar (SAR) at high-resolution, interferometer and full-polarization, which has been developed by the Institute of Remote Sensing and Digital Earth (RADI), Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), funded by the CAS Large Research Infrastructures. From 2009 to 2015, the first-stage project has been accomplished. X-SAR system was successfully implemented to an operational SAR in X-band with high spatial resolution (up to 0.5 meter). A flexible internal calibrator has been integrated in X-SAR radar, which can be guaranteed the outstanding performance of image products, regardless of operated on in-flight data acquisition and on laboratory measurements. All calibration results of X-SAR system were emphasized the quantitative measurement capabilities. The radiometric enhanced products of intensity change detection has been supplemented, in which X-SAR calibrated images products at 0.5 meter spatial resolution have be already achieved the image located precision less than 2.7 meter and long-term radiometric stability better than 0.5dB. This paper summarizes the behavior of the internal calibrator, meantime describes the essential results of the internal and external calibration.

articleTitle: Nulls placement of phased array radar with single receiving channel for ECCM
abstract: Some phased array radars have only one receiving channel behind the whole antenna, and the signal from each antenna element of the array cannot be measured respectively. So many traditional array processing algorithms for nulls placement are not suitable for these radars to suppress the jamming signals from the different directions. A new model of nulls placement for this kind of radar is developed in the paper. After the approximate nulls come into being, through the small movement of nulls in their own nearby zones, the output of jamming power is reduced by iterative steps for optimization. In this way the nulls are exactly placed at the angles of jamming arrival so as to minimize the jamming power into the radar. In the end, the simulation results show the validity of this method. It is important for ECCM (Electronic Counter-countermeasures) applications.

Author Keywords: phased array radar with single receiving channel

articleTitle: A novel parameter and state joint estimation method of reentry ballistic targets
abstract: In this paper, the reentry phase tracking problem of the ballistic missile for the ground-based anti-missile radar is considered, and a novel parameter and state joint estimation method based on the unscented Kalman filter (UKF) is present. The innovation of this thesis lies in using the Dynamic-Singer model and the 1st order Markov model as the state model of the UKF. The Dynamic-Singer model consists of the reentry ballistic missile dynamic model which is built on the earth-centered-earth-fixed (ECEF) coordinate system and the Singer model which is introduced to describe the maneuverability characteristic of the target in the reentry phase. The 1st order Markov process is used to model the mass-to-drag ratio which is an unknown parameter and usually important to the target recognizing. The presented method is easy to use for data process engineers in the practical radar system, and its performance is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Fuzzy association of vessel targets in heterogeneous remote sensing images
abstract: The purpose of this letter is to present a method for data association in spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and optical vessel detection reports. Firstly, we analyze the track prediction uncertainty which makes the association problem difficult to be solved. Then in the condition with speed information unknown in detection reports, we use the vessel's sailing angle based on the dead reckoning and multiple features to get a fuzzy correlation matrix. In the matching step, the well-known global nearest neighbor (GNN) criterion is used to get a optimal matching. The experiment results in different condition show that the proposed method is efficient for data association in large-scale maritime surveillance.

articleTitle: Advances and breakthroughs in radars and phased-arrays
abstract: Moore's Law is slowing down but the transistor density is expected to increase by ~50 in the next 30 years while the power consumed by each transistors will decrease by ~75. Potential further continuation of Moore's Law via: 1. Spintronics - which could revolutionize computer architecture away from von Neumann model, 2. Memristors - which potentially allows one to do what human brain does in a shoe box instead of a computer the size of a city requiring a nuclear power plant, 3. Graphene with 1 Thz clock speed, and 4. Quantum Computing. Advances made in metamaterials. Iowa Un. demonstrated 6 dB stealthing from 8-10 GHz using thin, stretchable metamaterial skin that can be conformal on target. The Army Research Laboratory in Adelphi MD has developed a low profile λ/20 thick metamaterial 250-505 MHZ antenna. Kymeta demonstrated December 2013 transmission to satellites and back using laptop size 20 and 30 GHz antennas which use metamaterial resonators to effect the phase shifting. For the first time a clear explanation of how this antenna works given. PATRIOT has GaN active electronically scanned arrays (AESAs) which gives 360° coverage without mechanical rotation. AMDR handles >30 times more targets and has >30 times sensitivity of SPY-1D(V). Can now put a 32 element 60 GHz T/R array on a chip. All the RF circuitry for mm-wave radars is put on a chip. Such radars and phased arrays could cost just a few dollars. Major advances in printed flexible electronic circuits with diodes operating at 1.6 GHz and the potential for operation at 2.4GHz, the Wi-Fi band. A low profile dual polarized tightly coupled dipole antenna (TCDA) has been developed which provides a 20:1 bandwidth and has λ/40 thickness. The latest type of phased array is the MIMO radar phased array which has been shown to provide orders of magnitude better accuracy and resolution as well as better GMTI performance than conventional arrays. However, as summarized here, more recently this author has shown that conventional arrays can do just as well if properly used without suffering MIMO's signal processing load and waveform design problems.

articleTitle: Unambiguous detection of migrating targets with wideband radar in Gaussian clutter
abstract: In this paper the problem of unambiguous moving target detection using wideband radar is considered. Doppler ambiguities, which are present in the low pulse repetition frequency mode, are transformed into ambiguous sidelobes of targets and clutter using range migration effect. However, the level of these sidelobes is typically high, such that standard detectors suffer from false alarms generated by the ambiguous sidelobes of real targets. To remove these false alarms two new detectors assuming Gaussian distribution of clutter and exploiting high resolution spectral estimation are developed. These detectors are based on spectral estimation obtained with non-parametric Iterative Adaptive Approach from spectrum analysis and satisfy bounded false alarm condition. Approach to reduce the number of reference cells for covariance matrix estimation is discussed. The benefits of the proposed detectors are demonstrated via numerical simulations showing improvement over existing algorithms.

articleTitle: MIMO radars and their conventional equivalents
abstract: This paper is given in tutorial form using a simple explanation starting from basics of phased arrays and how they work. Physical insight into MIMO is then given. No heavy math used. It has been shown in the literature that MIMO thin/full array radars can provide orders of magnitude better resolution and accuracy than conventional radars. The thin/full array consisted of two collocated parallel linear arrays of N elements each. One is a thin array and the other a full array having spacings respectively of Nλ/2 and λ/2 with the thin one used for transmit and the full for receive. We show how to use the same thin/full arrays in conventional radars to do as well and also without grating lobes (GLs). Also covered are full/thin array equivalents. Detailed are the monostatic MIMO full array radar and its Skolnik ubiquitous equivalent and a machine gunning equivalent. The performance of these systems against jammers is summarized. A simple physical explanation is given of why the Cramer-Rao bound provides a V2 better angle accuracy for the MIMO monostatic full array than the conventional ubiquitous array equivalent and why this result does not apply for the machine gunning equivalent. It has been also shown in the literature that a MIMO thin/full array airborne GMTI radar can provide a better minimum detectable velocity (MDV) than a conventional one. We show how the same MIMO thin/full array can be used in a conventional GMTI radar system to provide the same advantages as the MIMO system re coherence dwell time and aperture size and thus should provide the same MDV. The operation, waveforms, detection sensitivities, use of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) for angle estimation and detection, and resolutions of these systems are detailed. We show that the signal processing load for the MIMO radar system can typically be much larger than for its conventional equivalents. There is also usually a more difficult waveform design problem with MIMO. Finally we present potential practical applications of the MIMO radar.

articleTitle: A group target track correlation algorithm based on systematic error estimation
abstract: Aiming to solve the track refined correlation problem of the group targets with systematic errors, based on the characteristics of the group tracks, an algorithm of track refined correlation with in group targets based on systematic error compensation is proposed with the error estimation technique and the track correlation technique. In this algorithm, the groups are identified with the tracks of the sensors based on the circulatory threshold model firstly. Secondly, the preparatory correlation groups with the nearest resolving state are searched or established based on group track state identification model. Thirdly, the final systematic errors are estimated with group track systematic error estimation model and error validation model. What is more, the error compensation is completed. Finally, group track refined correlation is done with the traditional track correlation algorithms. The analysis results of the simulation data show that the general performance of this algorithm, which can meet the engineering requirement of the track refined correlation of the group targets with systematic errors very well, is better than that of fuzzy track alignment-correlation algorithm based on target topological information, track alignment-correlation algorithm based on iterative closest track and modified weighted track correlation algorithm.

Author Keywords: Group Track Systematic Error Estimation Model

articleTitle: Generalized dimension spectrum features based classification method for aircraft
