abstract: A new efficient method is proposed for measuring the fractal dimensionality are presented. The efficiency of the method is corroborated by numerous results of digital processing of optical, radar-natural, and synthesized images including soft ones.

articleTitle: The anti-jamming method based on front-back-edge tracking of VGPO jamming
abstract: Tracking radar can provide the range, velocity and angle measured values of the target continuously, smoothly and accurately. Velocity gate pull off (VGPO) jamming is an active deception jamming aiming at velocity automatic tracking system. The system of Pulse Doppler (PD) tracking radar may face VGPO jamming, so a new method of anti-jamming is proposed in this paper. First of all, it judges the jamming towing direction from the velocity gate moving acceleration, then tracks the target velocity using front-back-edge tracking method in Doppler domain. Using the front-edge tracking method counters jamming while jamming is posterior to the target echo, and using the back-edge tracking method counters the jamming while jamming is in front of target echo. The simulation results show that this method has good effectiveness of anti-VGPO jamming.

articleTitle: DOA estimation exploiting extended co-array of coprime array
abstract: In this paper, we propose a Vectorized Conjugate Augmented MUSIC (VCAM) method which can construct an extended co-array named as diff-sum co-array. The diff-sum co-array comprises not only the difference co-array but also the sum co-array. Taking coprime array as the array model, we find all the holes in the difference co-array can be filled up by the elements in the sum co-array so that the diff-sum co-array contains more consecutive lags than the difference co-array. In particular, we discuss the complementarity between the difference and sum sets, and derive consecutive range of the diff-sum co-array. Simulations verify the effectivity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A wideband 45 degree polarized electrical scanning antenna array manufactured by 3D printing with metals
abstract: 3D printing is a new technology in antenna manufacturing. In this paper, a wideband 45 degree polarization antenna array is designed and manufactured by metallic 3d printing technology. With the employment of a bulkhead between two ridges, the antenna dimension in the scanning plane is reduced, thus a ±30° scanning capability is achieved. The operating bandwidth of the antenna covers X and Ku bands with 2 octave bandwidth.

articleTitle: A novel radar waveform based on space-frequency coding compatible with directional communication
abstract: This paper presents an integration waveform of radar and communication based on the multi-antenna system. The communication data are emitted by utilizing space-frequency coding on the transmit antenna array. By using beamforming technology in the subarray level, wide area detecting as MIMO (multiple-input-multiple-output) radar and directional communication with the cooperative target in the main lobe can be achieved simultaneously. The simulation results confirm that the signal proposed is able to obtain radar detection capacity and reliable communication.

articleTitle: The method of InSAR/INS integrated navigation
abstract: This paper presents the concept and method of InSAR aided INS navigation. InSAR interferometric phase is sensitive to the attitude of the platform and the terrain height, so it can be used to improve the precision of navigation substantially. InSAR/INS integrated navigation system can be used on the flight vehicle navigation and it can satisfy complicated topography and long-distance accurate autonomous navigation. The technical route of InSAR/INS integrated navigation system is discussed in detail in this article. We can obtain the location shift of azimuth and range by matching two interference fringes, one is produced by InSAR system and another is generated by reference path and digital elevation database. And the simulation results indicate the precise and efficient of the matching algorithm. With the aid of the location shift we can inverse the attitude and position information of the platform. The location shift and the IMU information are set to the all-state combined filter to obtain the navigation output.

articleTitle: Miniature high resolution FMCW SAR system
abstract: The paper presents a miniature FMCW SAR and its flight trial. Firstly, the system diagram and some challenges in realization are introduced. Then, an integrative antenna is designed and simulated. To keep miniature, a hybrid DDS+PLL structure is used to generate wideband FMCW signal. To meet the requirements of real-time processing and high-speed mass data store, a signal processor is presented and the mapping from imaging algorithm onto processor is also developed. Finally, the good performance of the Mini-SAR is shown by the flight trial.

articleTitle: Wide transmit beamforming for the subarrays in MIMO radar
abstract: MIMO radar based on subarrays in transmission can achieve superior performance compared with the conventional phased-array radar and the MIMO radar with omni-directional transmission, since it combines the advantages of these two radars. In this paper we consider the wide transmit beamforming synthesis for the subarrays in MIMO radar. We propose an adaptive gradient algorithm to optimize the transmit beampattern for the subarrays. The resulted beampattern can cover the entire wide observation area in the mainlobe and simultaneously have low mainlobe ripple and low sidelobe level. Simulation results have been provided to verify the effectiveness of this proposed method.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional imaging performance analysis of one-stationary bistatic circular SAR
abstract: Due to the circular trajectory and 360° integration angle of the moving radar, the one-stationary bistatic circular synthetic aperture radar (OS-BCSAR) system has the serious wavenumber coupling of the target echo data in comparison to the one-stationary bistatic linear SAR (OS-BLSAR), which affects the three-dimensional (3D) imaging performance of the OS-BCSAR. First, the OS-BCSAR imaging geometry is built, and 3D wavenumber of the target echo data is derived. Based the derived wavenumber, 3D resolution of the OS-BCSAR system is discussed, which can provide a basis for the 3D OS-BCSAR imaging. Finally, simulation results are shown to prove the correctness of 3D imaging performance analysis.

Author Keywords: one-stationary bistatic circular synthetic aperture radar

articleTitle: Detection of a well-characterized signal in persistent clutter
abstract: In scenarios involving persistent signal and clutter, such as occur in passive radar applications in urban environments containing fixed commercial transmitters, subspaces of clutter and signals of interest may be well characterized. With signal and clutter subspaces known, but not necessarily linearly independent, standard matched-subspace detectors based on generalized likelihood ratio test project measurement data into the orthogonal complement of the clutter subspace, thereby ignoring any signal energy that falls into the clutter subspace. This paper proposes a model on the distribution of the clutter subspace that enables signal energy in the clutter subspace to be exploited by the detector. Therefore, a combined detector making use of full signal subspace is proposed, which improves the detection performance with sensible weight formula. Its effectiveness is verified by the receiving operating characterized curves.

articleTitle: Persymmetric adaptive target detection without training data in collocated MIMO radar
abstract: For adaptive target detection in a collocated Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar with a symmetrical spaced linear array, we propose an adaptive detector according to the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) criterion. The proposed detector does not need training data and exploits the persymmetric structures in the receive signal. Simulation results show that the proposed detector significantly outperforms the conventional detectors when the number of the transmit waveform samples is moderate.

articleTitle: Research on high-resolution wide-swath SAR based on microwave photonics
abstract: Microwave photonics becomes a new and potential technology with the advantage of wide bandwidth, high speed and parallel processing, which can overcome the electronic bottleneck problem of traditional devices and achieve high performance. In this paper, the SAR system based on microwave photonics is proposed, which achieves high resolution and wide swath simultaneously. According to this architecture, an example of high-resolution wide-swath SAR system is designed. The simulation results prove the technical feasibility.

articleTitle: Integrated radar signal processing using FPGA dynamic reconfiguration
abstract: With the development of radar signal processing, integration of radar communication and guidance design on the hardware becomes popular. Dynamic partial reconfiguration of FPGA can reconfigure part of its logic resource at run time. In this article, an integrated radar signal processing hardware platform was designed, on which both LFM waveform and FSK waveform were processed with method of FPGA dynamic partial reconfiguration. FPGA receives the partial reconfiguration file transferred from host computer and reconfigures part of its logic changing the function. FPGA can be time-multiplexed by using FPGA dynamic partial reconfiguration which can reduce resource usage and power dissipation.

articleTitle: A novel sidelobe suppression method based on the CLEAN algorithm for bi-phase codes pulse compression
abstract: In the low probability of intercept radar, the sidelobe suppression filter is extensively employed to solve the problem that weak targets are usually buried in the range sidelobes of strong targets. However, the sidelobes cannot be suppressed effectively with conventional sidelobe suppression filter. A technique of sidelobe suppression filter for bi-phase coded signal suppresses the sidelobes to expected values, but new sidelobes emerges. To deal with the above phenomenon, a new sidelobe suppression method which combines the technique of sidelobe suppression filter and the CLEAN algorithm is proposed. The weak targets buried in the sidelobes of the strong targets can be discovered after applying the proposed method. Moreover, the new sidelobes and false targets produced in the process of sidelobe suppression can be eliminated. The distance and amplitude of each target could be estimated accurately and robustly. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that a significant improvement is achieved with the proposed method for weak targets detection.

articleTitle: Optimal guided search based on average discovering time for phased array radar
abstract: Aimed at optimizing the guided search with forewarning information for phased array radar, this paper builds the target's average discovering time model based on the probability of the target locating at each beam position. The optimal search parameters are got under the condition of single target and multi-targets respectively. Simulations prove that this optimal method achieves better search performance than the traditional sequential scanning.

articleTitle: Preferential optimal antenna placement for MIMO radar under the situation of multiple surveillance regions
abstract: In this paper, a preferential optimization problem of antenna placement for a distributed Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) radar is studied. Considering multiple surveillance regions, the radar performances of preferential regions need to be improved and more choices of placement schemes for desired performance need to be provided. Therefore, we use the Particle Swarm Optimiztion (PSO) with reference point to solve the antenna placement problems. By setting reference points, the performance values of preferential surveillance regions will converge to reference points and reach our requirement. Then, we analyse the performance of proposed algorithm. Finally, numerical results are provided to verify the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Estimation of source number based on power-inversion and adaptive threshold in colored noise
abstract: The source number estimation is an important issue in space spectrum estimation. However, the performance of traditional estimation algorithms will degrade severely when applied into colored noise. To overcome this problem, a new method based on power-inversion and adaptive threshold is proposed. In the proposed method, the power-inversion algorithm is firstly applied to form array beam pattern with nulls in the direction of sources. Subsequently, the beam pattern is modified and the adaptive threshold is determined by sliding window processing for the modified beam pattern. Finally, the number of sources is obtained through finite difference method. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Fast integral method for near-field cross section imaging at millimeter wave
abstract: Near-field cross section imaging is an important issue for near filed radar imaging. Conventional methods always transform the recorded data to the frequency wavenumber domain and utilize interpolation and fast Fourier transforms (FFT) to reconstruct image. Since the interpolation accuracy significantly affects the image quality especially when the spatial spectrum data is highly curving in the case of wideband millimeter wave. To avoid interpolation and consider the calculation efficiency, a fast integral imaging method is proposed. The imaging formula is derived from the echo signal model. A two dimensional integral obtained by back projection theory is transformed into a one-dimensional FFT and a one-dimensional integral which guarantee accuracy and efficiency. Simulation is carried out to certify the effectiveness and efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: The waveform design of random hopping frequency based on "S" curve
abstract: To improve the anti-interference capability of high range resolution radar, the random hopping frequency signal is required. A waveform design method of random hopping frequency signal based on "S" curve is presented. Firstly, the random hopping frequency signal with low peak side lobe is obtained by optimization. Then the frequency distribution is analyzed and fitted by "S" curve. The ambiguity function of RHF signal based on different window functions is evaluated. The results show that the random hopping frequency signal has low peak sidelobe level, small mainlobe broadening, strong anti-interference capability and low implementation cost, which indicates its high practical value in real applications.

articleTitle: A fast target detection framework for SAR imagery
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fast target detection framework for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery. The crucial issue of this method is the potential target area map which is obtained from a preliminary screening. With reference to the potential target area map, we can conduct local constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection only in the potential target areas as well as eliminate the potential target pixels from the estimation of the local clutter distribution. The experiment results show that the proposed fast target detection framework not only has high detection accuracy but also has a great improvement on efficiency.

articleTitle: Effect of specular reflection on radar detection
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: radar imaging; synthetic aperture radar; radar signal processing; radar detection; object detection; target tracking; radar clutter; array signal processing; Doppler radar; and radar resolution.

articleTitle: A novel tracking algorithm of hypersonic target
abstract: Aimed at the near space hypersonic target of high speed and strong maneuvering, a strong tracking square-root Cubature Kalman filter algorithm based on normalized residuals is proposed. The algorithm is based on the square-root Cubature Kalman filter, introducing the idea of strong tracking filter. In view of the shortcoming of residuals asymmetry caused by the different order of magnitude of the residuals, the normalized processing of residuals is used to make the information equilibrium of the residuals and maximize extraction of the information, which improves accuracy, instantaneity, and robustness. The algorithm is applied to the near space hypersonic target as a new method, the simulation results show effectiveness the algorithm.

articleTitle: A novel ionospheric clutter mitigation method through time-frequency image processing based on ridgelet analysis
abstract: For Ionospheric clutter is non-stationary and very strong, targets submerged in it is too difficult to extract. The detection performance of High Frequency Surface Wave Radar (HFSWR) is influenced. Ridgelet analysis is a tool for analyzing non-stationary signals and can separate lines with different directions and scales in a 2D image. Therefore, this paper presents a new method which applies ridgelet analysis to time-frequency image of radar signal to mitigate the clutter. The results show that this method can mitigate the clutter effectively, and the target submerged in clutter can be extracted well. When the target submerged in clutter and have low signal-to-clutter ratio, about 15~20dB improvement can be get after the processing.

articleTitle: Kullback-Leibler divergence based range-Doppler spectrum region partition method for OTHR
abstract: A Doppler-range spectrum region segmentation method for Over-the-Horizon Radar (OTHR) is proposed as a preprocessor for the following signal processing. The method derives from the well-known Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence which measures dissimilarity between the sea clutter and atmosphere noise. By thresholding the bias of KL map it is estimated by a statistical and variational multiphase level set method. Compared with the Otsu method and the deviation based method by experiments used synthetic data and real data, the proposed algorithm shows a better performance which is robust to the interference of targets and speckled noise.

articleTitle: Study on broadband direction finding system with interferometer based on amendatory electric baseline
abstract: The direction finding system with interferometer has the features of high precision, high sensitivity, strong anti-jamming performance and low time-consuming, which is used widely in the field of electromagnetism environment monitoring, electronic countermeasure, radar, sonar and navigation. The direction finding system with interferometer has high requirements on the phase stability in each channel and the precision of baseline between antennas. Research shows that the error of baseline between antennas has significant influence on system. A method i s proposed to calculate electric baseline with the phase calibration data. It resolves the problem efficaciously which is caused by antenna phase center offset and improves the precision of direction. The method is simple engineering and efficient.

articleTitle: A two-step detector based on point spread function feature for multi-channel SAR-GMTI radar
abstract: When the energy of a moving target's main-lobe and that of side-lobes are both evidently greater than the average lever of residual clutter plus noise, a moving target may be detected as multiple targets, i.e., the side-lobes may be detected as another targets, which often results in the overload of radar system. However, the side-lobes may not be removed by adopting the conventional detectors exploiting the amplitude or amplitude-phase features for the fact that they have the similar phase feature to the main-lobe. To address this issue, we propose a new two-step detector based on point spread function (PSF) feature for Multi-channel SAR-GMTI Radar to eliminate this kind of repetitive detection for a potential target. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by the real dual-channel air-borne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data for ground moving target indication (GMTl).

articleTitle: A comb feature for the analysis of ship classification in high resolution SAR imagery
abstract: In the context of maritime surveillance from high resolution SAR imagery, this paper illustrates a study of ship classification, together with a new feature named `comb' suggested to solve the problem. The proposed comb feature presents the added value in application to distinguish between container ship, tank ship, and cargo ship. It is based on the analysis on radar cross section (RCS) statistic of the ship target related to the ship structure. Besides, a related local RCS (LRCS) is proposed to classify three kinds of ships. The data for experiments is made of TerraSAR-X images.

articleTitle: A sparse representation and GTD model parameter estimation based multiband radar signal coherent compensation method
abstract: In the traditional coherent compensation methods, the scattering center number and the overlapped frequency band data are two essential conditions which severely restrict the range of application. In this paper, depending on the sparsity of the scattering centers and the GTD(geometrical theory of diffraction) model, the parameter estimation is seen as a sparse representation problem here, and it is likely to obtain high accuracy estimation without knowing the scattering center number. The method in this paper gives two equations to estimate the incoherent parameters after deducing the relation between subbands, which does not need the overlapped frequency data. Applying the proposed method on simulated data, the results show that it can achieve coherent compensation precisely.

articleTitle: A novel method of DOA estimation on sparse uniform circular array
abstract: We propose a beamspace transform method to estimate direction-of-arrival(DOA) of coherent signals on sparse uniform circular array(UCA). By incorporating necessary phase modes into the beamspace steering vector and introducing a phase shift matrix before weight vectors, a conjugate symmetric beamspace steering vector is rebuilt based on phase mode excitation, therefore spatial smoothing can be applied to deal with coherent signals and root-MUSIC is also available to decrease computational load. What's more, spatial smoothing also improves the performance of resolution under condition of low SNR(signal to noise ratio) or fewer snapshots because it doubles the data amount. These performance merits are verified by computer simulations.

articleTitle: An improved approach to robust capon beamforming with enhanced performance
abstract: In this paper, the approach of robust Capon beam-forming (RCB) in the presence of steering vector mismatch is studied. A new method to enhance the robustness is presented. More specifically, it is proposed herein to remove the component of the desired signal from the array covariance matrix by estimating the corresponding steering vector and signal power, such that the influence caused by the presence of desired signal in the training data can be reduced, especially in the case of high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Furthermore, the uncertainties involved in the resulting interference-plus-noise covariance matrix estimate is taken into account by formulating a min-max optimization problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the performance of the RCB algorithm can be improved by the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Design and research of an UWB 45deg oblique polarized antenna array
abstract: A 45deg oblique polarized 3:1 bandwidth ±30deg scan antenna array is designed. The antenna is the printed log-periodic antenna made by dielectric substrate, and feed by a semirigid coaxial line. It has some advantages such as little weight, easy manufacture, high accuracy and consistency. The simulation method of the antenna and array is introduced in detail. The simulation results show the antenna array can achieve 3:1 bandwidth ±30deg scan at horizontal direction. Some antenna cells are made and measured. Accord to the VSWR measured results, some research and improvement is done with the antenna.

articleTitle: Multichannel L-band radar detection of fixed and moving targets in sparse foliage
abstract: Foliage Penetration Radar requires ultra wide band waveform and component design to efficiently detect targets under foliage. UWB designs are difficult at long wavelength, and have severe RF regulation compliance issues. When the foliage is sparse and the scattering loss is reduced, it is feasible to design systems in L-band where RF spectrum is available. A preliminary design approach addresses detection of both fixed and moving targets in sparse foliage.

articleTitle: GPU-accelerated mismatched filter for analog TV-based passive radar
abstract: Passive radar exploits third-party commercial transmitters such as frequency modulated signals, television (TV) signals and navigation signals to detect, locate and track targets. In this paper, for the considerations of both large transmitting power and wide coverage area, analog TV signal is selected as the transmitter of the passive radar. Analog TV signal consists of audio signal and visual signal. Audio signal with the ambiguity function like a pushpin can be viewed as a perfect transmitter, whereas video signal which is periodical in time-domain, resulting in the existence of high ambiguous range side-lobes, is not the case. In general, traditional mismatched filter based on only visual signal addresses the undesired problem at the cost of the loss of signal-noise-ratio (SNR) of target. In this paper, to suppress ambiguous range side-lobes and reduce the loss of SNR to the most degree, a modified mismatched filter based on visual signal and audio signal instead of single visual signal is presented. Furthermore, the detailed parallel implementations based on graphic processing unit (GPU) of the proposed method are described for the purpose of real-time processing. The performance of the proposed method is demonstrated via several simulations.

articleTitle: GPU parallel acceleration of target detection in passive radar system
abstract: This paper presents an effective parallel implementation of target detection which uses NVIDIA CUDA technology for parallel processing in passive radar system. The implementation includes parallel three level detection thresholds, namely noise threshold, peak threshold and range Doppler threshold. Algorithm was tested in the Passive Coherent Location System developed at Wuhan University utilizes commercial CMMB television transmitters as "illuminators of opportunity". Simulated and experimental measurement data were used to verify the parallel performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Robust intra-pulse modulation recognition via sparse representation
abstract: Aimed at the problem that overlapped signals and noise interference in complex electromagnetic environment cause recognition rate declined, this paper proposed a robust radar signal intra-pulse modulation recognition method, instantaneous frequency and frequency spectrum feature are extracted for online dictionary learning which represent each type of modulated pulse, and recognition results are acquired by selecting the minimum residual of sparse reconstruction, the experiment results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can obtain higher recognition accuracy with low SNR and overlapped pulses condition, which is more applicable for the practical applications.

articleTitle: Robust widely linear beamforming against look direction error
abstract: A class of robust beamformers that are insensitive to the look direction error is herein proposed by employing the second-order noncircularity of the signal-of-interest (SOI) in a widely linear framework. The first method is a widely linear extension of the constrained Hung-Turner beamformer, which exploits the prior knowledge about the interference directions. The second method represents a widely linear version of the constrained generalized sidelobe canceller, which uses a derivative constraint on the blocking matrix. The third method uses the covariance matrix reconstruction technique from a widely linear perspective. Simulation results are included to illustrate the robustness performance of the proposed beamformers in terms of output signal-to-interference-plus noise ratio versus input signal-to-noise ratio and snapshot number.

articleTitle: An improved MFSK waveform for low-cost automotive radar
abstract: In this paper, an improved waveform design method based on the multiple frequency shift keying (MFSK) is proposed for automotive radar. In this proposed method, the waveform is constituted by three stepped frequency signals, which generates two different ambiguous ranges. The precise range and velocity of target are computed with the two ambiguous ranges above. Compared to the common MFSK waveform, with the same computation load and the same maximum detection range, the proposed waveform can detect the velocity and range of targets more precisely on the condition of the same signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). We also demonstrate the feasibility by means of simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: DOA estimation of mixed signals under unknown mutual coupling
abstract: An efficient method to deal with direction of arrival (DOA) estimation of mixed signals under unknown mutual coupling is proposed. Several groups of signals are included in the mixed signals, where signals in the same group are coherent while in different groups are independent with each other. Our proposed method realizes high utilization ratio of array sensors based on the independence of different groups. By using subspace smoothing and multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm, DOA and mutual coupling coefficients are estimated sequentially, where some transformation of steering vector is applied to reduce computational amount. Simulations verify the effectiveness of proposed method.
